constraints.description: European Postdoctoral Fellowships must have a standard duration of between 12 and 24 months.

Global Postdoctoral Fellowships require an outgoing phase of minimum 12 and maximum 24 months in a non-associated Third Country, plus a mandatory 12-month return phase to a host organisation based in an EU Member State or a Horizon Europe Associated Country.
Applications must be made jointly by the researcher and a beneficiary in the academic or non-academic sector, and fellowships require the researcher to undertake international mobility.

For European Postdoctoral Fellowships, secondments cannot exceed half of the requested duration of the action (excluding any additional period for a non-academic placement) and must be in line with project objectives.

For Global Postdoctoral Fellowships, optional secondments are permitted for up to half of the outgoing phase; a maximum of three months of such secondments may be spent at the start at the beneficiary and counts as part of the outgoing phase.
Secondments cannot take place during the mandatory twelve-month return period to the host organisation in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country.

Postdoctoral Fellowships may include an additional period of up to six months for a placement at the end of the project in a non-academic-sector organisation established in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country; the request must be an integral part of the proposal, explain its added value, and is subject to evaluation.

If the non-academic placement does not meet the requirements (e.g. taking place in an academic organisation or in a Third Country), the proposal will be evaluated without taking the placement into account, which might affect the final score.

A Career Development Plan must be established jointly by the supervisor(s) and the researcher, covering research objectives and the researcher's training and career needs; it must be submitted as a project deliverable at the beginning of the action and updated when needed.

Training activities must integrate key transferable skills and competences common to all fields, including digital ones (e.g. generative AI), and foster Open Science, knowledge valorisation, innovation/entrepreneurship where applicable, and good scientific conduct such as research integrity.

Specific eligibility conditions apply to MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships in research areas covered by the Euratom Research and Training Programme; only organisations active in nuclear research established in an EU Member State or a country associated to the Euratom Programme are eligible in that area, supported by an indicative annual Euratom contribution of EUR 1 million.
The call is single-stage with a submission deadline of 9 September 2026; the call opened on 9 April 2026.
The indicative available call budget for 2026 is EUR 59,857,539.
